article.title: Awaiting answers: On the student protests in Jharkhand
article.quote: The youth of Jharkhand deserve not only a fair recruitment system but also a government that diversifies their options for gainful employment.
body_paragraphs: When the route up the economic ladder in society is limited to an ever-narrowing range of options in the public sector, and the process of gaining entry through entrance examinations becomes tainted, angst and agitation are the results. This is why students in Jharkhand have been protesting in Ranchi for over three weeks.

The trigger was the July 2 result of the JPSC Combined Civil Services preliminary examination, which shortlisted 2,204 candidates from about 3.5 lakh aspirants for 103 posts. Aspirants pointed to undisclosed category-wise cut-offs, oddities in the merit list, and an ostensibly successful candidate who had attempted fewer than half the questions.

Both student platforms want the cancellation of disputed exams, a CBI investigation and prosecution of officials, besides the reconstitution of commissions. The government has responded with raids and arrests, which might help assuage the agitating students but could leave honest candidates in the lurch.
The rot in the exam system is deep-rooted. Cycles have been bunched up many times, which has eroded trust in the recruitment process.
